label: Newton iteration formula
subgoals: See each step as a tangent-line root

slice.rule: From a guess $x_n$, follow the tangent line at $(x_n, f(x_n))$ down to the axis: $x_{n+1} = x_n - \dfrac{f(x_n)}{f'(x_n)}$, valid while $f'(x_n) \neq 0$. Each step is the root of the linearization of $f$ at $x_n$.
slice.note: The sign matters: it is minus $f/f'$. A plus sign walks away from the root.

slice.rule: Near a simple root the method converges quadratically: the number of correct digits roughly doubles each step, so three or four steps usually give calculator precision.
The method has no root to find when $f'(x_n) = 0$ (a horizontal tangent never meets the axis), it can jump far away from a poor starting guess, and it can cycle between values without settling.

examples.says: no real root at all: the iterates wander forever
each step doubles the distance from the root $0$

slice.note: Check $|x_{n+1} - x_n|$ shrinking; if it grows or repeats, change the starting guess.
